correctness.rationale: The all-size face decomposition was checked directly; the initial three-simplex nerve is a circle, each defect simplex attaches along a generating circle, and the pair relative homology calculation gives the sum map on Z^(p+q). Each additional tetrahedron meets the preceding complex along its entire boundary; its signed attaching vector is e_i-f_j. A spanning-tree incidence minor is unimodular, so the image is the entire integral sum-zero lattice, leaving free H3 of rank (p-1)(q-1) and no other reduced homology. Van Kampen, Hurewicz and homological Whitehead upgrade this to a homotopy wedge. An independent standard-library checker matches complete face sets, reduced mod-two homology, and integral minors for nine instances. Finite checks do not prove the infinity of cases; the symbolic argument does.

value.rationale: The family probes a natural minimal perturbation of complete tripartite graphs: deleting one matched cross-edge family can produce 2-spheres, but a second disjoint adjacent-part defect family creates a new 3-dimensional interaction. The exact rank (p-1)(q-1) counts the cycle lattice of the complete bipartite incidence graph of the defects. This gives a complete infinite-family integral homotopy classification, including the sharp contractible versus noncontractible threshold and independence from shore sizes; it is not just a relabeling or a single finite computation.
